newsitem.title: INDIA: At least 33 killed in India train blast.
newsitem.headline: At least 33 killed in India train blast.

text.p: At least 33 people were killed and 66 injured when a powerful bomb exploded on a passenger train in the northern Indian state of Punjab on Tuesday, hospital authorities and officials said.
"Thirty bodies are lying at the spot and three have died after being brought to the hospital," Avtar Singh Sekhon, senior medical officer at the Civil Hospital, Bhatinda, told Reuters by telephone.
Sekhon said 66 people were injured in the blast, of which 15 were seriously hurt.

Dilip Kumar, assistant inspector at Bhatinda police station, said the explosion occurred at a small railway station in the town of Lehrakhanna at around 2 p.m. (0830 GMT). Bhatinda is about 25 km (15 miles) from the site of the explosion.
Kumar said the blast, which occurred on the fourth carriage from the engine, blew off the roof of that coach.
One survivor, Dhanna Ram, said: "We were sitting and suddenly there was an ear-shattering explosion...after that there was complete silence. Then I heard people screaming, 'Fire! Fire!'
"When I regained consciousness, I saw my body wrapped in bandages," Ram, 60, told Reuters.
Local officials said the train was travelling from Bhatinda to the city of Ambala, 150 km (90 miles) to the northeast.
Bawa Ram Gupta, a surgeon at Bhatinda hospital, said patients were still being brought in and the death toll was likely to rise.
Tirath Ram, a hospital official, said the injured were brought to the hospital by the local residents of the area in tractor trolleys, mini buses and cars.
Punjab, one of India's most prosperous states, was rocked by a Sikh separatist insurgency in the 1980s. Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was assassinated by her Sikh bodyguards in 1984.

In August 1995, the state's chief minister Beant Singh was killed when a bomb planted in his chauffeur-driven car exploded. At least seven people were killed in March in a bomb blast in Punjab near a busy railway station.
Sikh militants fighting for an independent homeland have often targeted trains and buses.
No group has claimed responsibility for Tuesday's explosion.
Railway Minister Ram Vilas Paswan expressed deep shock and profound grief over the bombing, a government statement said.

More than 20,000 people have died in Punjab since discontent with New Delhi turned into an armed insurrection after Gandhi, in 1984, sent troops into the Golden Temple, Sikhdom's holiest shrine, to flush out armed militants holed up there.
